chief_complaint: cola-colored urine and swelling around my eyes
hpi_details: 22F presents with 2 days of dark, 'cola-colored' urine and swelling around her eyes in the morning. She had a severe sore throat 2 weeks ago that was not treated with antibiotics.

core_concepts: Nephritic syndrome presentation: hematuria, hypertension, edema, and mild-to-moderate proteinuria.
Typically occurs 1-3 weeks after Strep pharyngitis or 3-6 weeks after skin infection.
common_misconceptions: Assuming all red/brown urine is simply a UTI or stone (must look for dysmorphic RBCs or casts).
dangerous_errors: Missing the hypertension that accompanies acute nephritic syndrome.
management_principles: Supportive care, treat hypertension and edema, check ASO titer, low C3 levels.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Kidney Disease

reference_soap.subjective: 22F with recent untreated pharyngitis presents with gross hematuria and periorbital edema.
reference_soap.objective: BP 160/95. Periorbital edema present. Urinalysis: large blood, 1+ protein, RBC casts.
reference_soap.plan: Check ASO titer, C3/C4 complement, BMP. Treat BP with diuretics/calcium channel blockers if needed. Nephrology consult.

learning_objectives: Identify the classic features of acute nephritic syndrome.

teaching.one_liner: Cola-colored urine, periorbital edema, and hypertension following a recent sore throat, classic for nephritic syndrome.

must_ask.say: When did you first notice your urine looking cola-colored or brown?
Did you have a sore throat or a skin infection in the past few weeks?
Where have you noticed swelling, especially around your eyes in the morning?
Have you had any headaches or blurry vision that could be related to high blood pressure?
Has the amount of urine you're passing changed recently?

history.answer: My urine turned a dark cola color two days ago, and my face and eyes have been really puffy when I wake up.
It started two days ago out of nowhere, and every time I have gone to the bathroom since then, it has stayed that same dark brown color.
No, I have never had dark or bloody urine like this before in my life.
It looks dark brown and tea-colored, just like Coca-Cola, and I haven't seen any blood clots or stringy bits in it.
The color is dark throughout the entire stream from start to finish.
No, it doesn't hurt at all when I pee or when the dark urine comes out.
No, I haven't felt any pain in my sides, my lower back, or down toward my groin.
No burning, no stinging, and I don't feel a sudden urgent need to rush to the bathroom.
I don't have trouble starting to pee, the stream is normal, and my bladder feels completely empty afterwards.
Now that you mention it, I am definitely peeing less often and the amount seems smaller, plus the urine looks a bit frothy on top.
My eyelids and the area around my eyes are very puffy in the mornings, and my socks felt a little tighter around my ankles yesterday evening.
About two weeks ago, I had a terrible sore throat with swollen glands and fever, but I never went to the clinic or took antibiotics for it.
No, I haven't had any skin sores, scrapes, or impetigo bumps recently.
I had a fever during that throat infection two weeks ago, but right now I have no fever, chills, or night sweats.
I've had a dull throbbing headache since yesterday, but no blurry vision, chest pain, or shortness of breath.
history.topic: Headache and high blood pressure symptoms

history.answer: No, I haven't had any joint swelling, stiffness, or butterfly rashes across my cheeks.
No cough, and I certainly haven't coughed up any blood.
I feel more worn out and sluggish than usual, but my weight hasn't dropped.
No nosebleeds, no bleeding from my gums, and I don't bruise easily.
No, I haven't taken any blood thinners, aspirin, or anti-inflammatory drugs.
No, I haven't done any heavy workouts, run long distances, or had any injuries or falls lately.
No, I haven't eaten beets, blackberries, or taken any strange vitamins or colored medications.
My last menstrual period was two weeks ago and was normal; I am not on my period right now.
My periods come every twenty-eight days like clockwork, there is no chance I could be pregnant, and I use condoms for protection.
I have always been healthy with no chronic medical conditions, diabetes, or kidney trouble.
I have never had any surgeries and I have never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any regular prescription medications, over-the-counter pills, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to medications, foods, or anything else.
No one in my family has kidney disease, kidney stones, dialysis history, or early hearing loss.
I am a college senior living in a campus dormitory, and I don't work around dyes, rubbers, or industrial chemicals.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I might have a beer or glass of wine with friends once or twice a month, but nothing heavy.
I'm terrified that I might be bleeding internally somewhere inside my body.
I'm really worried that my kidneys might be failing or permanently damaged.
I was hoping you could run some blood and urine tests to figure out what's causing this.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 160/95 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert young woman in no acute distress, with visible puffiness around both eyes.
Bilateral periorbital edema without conjunctival pallor, scleral icterus, or conjunctival injection.
Posterior pharynx is clear without active erythema, tonsillar enlargement, or exudates.
No palpable cervical, submandibular, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Chest wall expansion is symmetric without tenderness.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally with no crackles, wheezes, or rhonchi.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Soft and non-tender throughout; no palpable masses, organomegaly, or suprapubic distension.
Trace pitting edema over both pretibial areas.
No petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, or active rashes noted.
